title: 10 Practical Commercial Lease Negotiation Tips
excerpt: A structured way for Australian business tenants to compare options, define priorities and negotiate with better information.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Commercial Lease Negotiation Tips | Your Office Space
metaDescription: Ten practical steps for comparing and negotiating an Australian commercial lease with clearer priorities and evidence.
body:
Good lease negotiation starts before the landlord issues documents. The aim is to understand the business need, create genuine options and record the commercial agreement clearly.

## 1. Start before time pressure builds

Allow time to review the current lease, inspect alternatives and obtain specialist advice.

## 2. Write the brief first

Document location, size, timing, budget, accessibility, services, parking and future-change requirements.

## 3. Compare more than one credible option

A shortlist helps you test availability and understand trade-offs. Do not create false competition.

## 4. Compare total occupancy cost

Include rent, outgoings, parking, fitout, relocation, incentives, review mechanisms and end-of-lease obligations.

## 5. Separate essential terms from preferences

Know where you can trade and where the business cannot compromise.

## 6. Confirm the premises can support the use

Check planning, access, services, building constraints and approvals with qualified advisers.

## 7. Test the rent-review mechanism

Model each review across the proposed term and options.

## 8. Address fitout and make-good together

Record landlord works, approvals, ownership, maintenance and reinstatement responsibilities.

## 9. Keep a written issues register

Track each proposal, counterproposal, open item and responsible party.

## 10. Use the right advisers

Tenant representation can coordinate the commercial process. A commercial property lawyer should review legal drafting, with financial, tax, planning and technical advice added where relevant.

Your Office Space can help you structure the brief, compare premises and prepare a clear commercial negotiation plan.
